data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2023 was GBP 380.805m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle shows a net adverse prioryear development of approximately GBP 3.9m (c.1.02% of opening reserves), i.e. a modest strengthening of reserves. Prioryear movements reflect a mix of forces: large natural catastrophe activity (notably Hurricane Ian and other secondary perils), geopolitical losses related to the Russia/Ukraine conflict, and ongoing recalibration of IBNR and case reserves. No single large quantified prioryear gross adjustment is reported in the text; the movement is derived from the gross claims development table.
raw_causal_phrases: a series of 'secondary perils' such as convective storms, straight line winds, winter freeze and widespread flooding
the conflict in Ukraine giving rise to exposure that spreads across both the 2021 and 2022 Years of Account
the 2021 Year of Account's loss was dominated by heightened catastrophic activity and the conflict in Ukraine
There was no provision for unexpired risks at 31 December 2023 (31 December 2022: GBP nil).
data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (PYD) was calculated from the gross claims development table (claims development triangle) on page 45. No single explicit sentence quantifying a gross PYD amount was found in the narrative; therefore the triangle was used (per permitted fallback rules). The triangle is presented in GBP '000; the PYD has been converted to millions. No granular LOBspecific prioryear reserve movements are provided in gross terms in the notes, so LOB movements are not reported. RITC activity does not appear to materially distort the triangle for the older years used, but if RITC were present it would reduce triangle reliability. Figures are rounded; confidence flagged where calculations (0.8) or direct extraction (1.0) were used.
